question: Stable sleeve realised yield vs the 4.3% kill hurdle and vs a top posted Canadian HISA
sleeve: Stable / low-risk (portfolios.json F1): Cash & T-bills / HISA 55%, Short-duration govt bonds 25%, Broad equity 20%

Cash & T-bills / HISA.source: retiresmarter.ca/banking/best-hisa-rates/ - Best high-interest savings rates in Canada; top everyday rate (Saven Financial, FirstOntario Credit Union, Oaken Financial, Home Bank / Home Trust, EQ Bank at 3.00%); page stamped November 24 2026

Short-duration govt bonds.source: bankofcanada.ca/rates/interest-rates/t-bill-yields/ - Selected treasury bill yields; Treasury bills 3 month secondary-market average yield

Broad equity dividend yield.source: ASSUMED - broad-market dividend yield; no committed source in repo. Tagged ASSUMED per the H3 rule; headline also reported with equity set to zero.

context_us_3m_tbill_pct.source: fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DTB3 - Fed H.15 3-Month Treasury Bill Secondary Market Rate, Discount Basis
context_us_3m_tbill_pct.note: USD context only; a CAD account converting into USD pays FX (1.75% flagged in the portfolios.json account-currency note; F5 open) which erases the 1.13pp pickup on a one-time conversion basis.

verdict: The stable sleeve's realised income yield (2.61% gross / 2.55% net of MER with the ASSUMED 1.50% equity dividend; 2.31% gross / 2.25% net cash-only) does not clear the 4.3% kill hurdle (below by about 1.7-2.0 pp) and undercuts a top posted HISA at 3.00%. The sleeve's 4-5% nominal target must therefore come from equity price appreciation, not yield - unguaranteed. A pure top HISA beats the sleeve on realised income. Modelled from live rates, not a measured return; F4 supplies historical total return. Equity dividend input is ASSUMED and isolated.
